title: Correct frictional force (F=1 N)
description: Essential: The answer must be 1 N, recognizing that the applied force is less than the maximum static friction between block and board, so the block does not slip and friction equals the applied force.

title: Correct frictional force (F=5 N)
description: Essential: The answer must be 3.5 N, recognizing that the applied force exceeds the maximum static friction, so kinetic friction acts and the system accelerates.

title: Correct time (F=8 N)
description: Essential: The answer must be 1 s, obtained from solving the relative motion between the block and the board.

title: Maximum static friction analysis
description: Important: The solution must correctly compute the maximum static friction between the block and board (4 N) and between the board and ground (2 N) to determine slipping conditions.

title: Newton's second law application
description: Important: For parts (2) and (3), the solution must correctly apply Newton's second law to both the block and the board separately to find accelerations.

title: Relative motion kinematics
description: Important: For part (3), the solution must set up the correct kinematic equation for the relative displacement between the block and the board.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All calculations should maintain consistent units (kg, m, s, N) without conversion errors.

title: Sign error in friction direction
description: Pitfall: Penalize if friction forces on the block or board are assigned incorrect directions relative to motion or applied force.

title: Confusing static and kinetic friction
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the solution incorrectly uses kinetic friction when static friction should apply (e.g., in part (1)) or vice versa.
